messages:
acme-eng: Hey — after we peered VPCs earlier our pods can no longer resolve the private service endpoint `api.internal.acmeapp.com`. curl returns NXDOMAIN from the app pod. Anyone seen this after a peering change?

anna_support: 🤔 can you paste output of `dig +short api.internal.acmeapp.com` from one of the failing pods and the cluster / pod `resolv.conf`? Also your VPC IDs and any hosted zone IDs you control.

acme-eng: sure. from a pod:
```
$ dig +short api.internal.acmeapp.com

; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +short api.internal.acmeapp.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 34567
```
and `/etc/resolv.conf` shows `nameserver 169.254.20.10` (node-local-dns), search: `default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local my-vpc.compute.internal`
VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (ours)
Hosted zone we own: Z3ACMEPRIVATE

anna_support: thanks. Two quick checks: 1) do you have a private hosted zone in YOUR account for `api.internal.acmeapp.com`? 2) is the service using a provider-owned private hosted zone (PrivateLink style) that gets associated into your VPC? If both exist, your private zone will shadow the provider zone.

miguel_infra: adding context — with interface endpoints / private DNS the endpoint owner has a hosted zone that is associated into customer VPCs. If a customer creates a different private hosted zone with the same name in their account (even if empty), Route53 will prefer the customer zone and the service records won't resolve. Common after infra changes (peering/migrations) when people recreate zones.

acme-eng: ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name api.internal.acmeapp.com` and got our zone listed: `Z3ACMEPRIVATE` owner: 123456789012, associated VPCs: vpc-0a1b2c3d only. We don't see the Redwood-owned hosted zone in our account.

anna_support: OK that lines up. Can you run `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z3ACMEPRIVATE` and show the VPC association block? Also check if you have any resolver rules (Route53 Resolver) forwarding that FQDN to a forwarder.

acme-eng: output shows VPCs: [{VPCRegion: us-east-1, VPCId: vpc-0a1b2c3d}]. No resolver rules in our account for that name.

miguel_infra: likely root cause: your private hosted zone name is shadowing the provider's zone. Two remediation paths:
- quick: delete or rename your private hosted zone for `api.internal.acmeapp.com` (if safe) so the provider-hosted zone records become visible in your VPC, or
- longer: ask the service owner (Redwood) to associate their provider private hosted zone into your VPC (they usually do when you enable private DNS), or
- workaround: create Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound rules to forward that domain to the service owner's DNS (if they provide a forwarder) — more complex.

samir_svc: to confirm this is shadowing, on one of your app nodes run `dig @<node-resolver-ip> api.internal.acmeapp.com +trace` and `kubectl exec -n web pod -- curl -v http://api.internal.acmeapp.com` while we watch logs. If you can share `tcpdump -n -i any port 53` from a node that would show whether the query hits the node-local cache or is stopped.

acme-eng: running `dig +trace` now — shows the query being answered by our private zone (NO RECORD). tcpdump attached (snippet):
```
13:02:01.123456 IP 10.0.12.34.35972 > 169.254.20.10.53: 12345+ A? api.internal.acmeapp.com. (45)
13:02:01.123491 IP 169.254.20.10.53 > 10.0.12.34.35972: 12345 NXDomain 0/0/0 (85)
```

anna_support: that NXDOMAIN from node-local-dns confirms a local/private zone answered the query. Since the provider-managed records are not present in your private zone, the lookup fails. Next step: Do you control any automation that created that private zone during onboarding? If yes, we recommend removing the zone or disassociating the VPC from it and allowing the provider-hosted zone to surface.

acme-eng: we do have automation. Oops. We'll try removing the zone (staging first). If we delete/rename the zone do we risk anything else? Any tips?

miguel_infra: Make sure no internal services rely on the custom records in that zone. If the zone is empty (only existed as a placeholder), deleting is safe. If you need to preserve records, export them to a different subdomain (eg `own.api.internal.acmeapp.com`) or move the records into the provider-hosted zone if you can coordinate with them.

eng-oncall-bot: Escalation: routed to eng-infra for visibility (case #INC-2026-583).

acme-eng: deleted the placeholder zone in staging and DNS now resolves correctly to the endpoint IPs. We'll roll to prod after a quick audit. Thanks everyone!

anna_support: awesome — glad that fixed it. :thumbsup: If prod still has issues after rollout, ping us and include `dig +short` and the `get-hosted-zone` output and we'll reopen the case.
